card: This pull request enables IPC in the 32-bit x86 (i686) CI test job. Previously, the i686 job was chosen to test building with IPC disabled, leaving 32-bit IPC untested. Compiler ABI issues on 32-bit architectures have previously caused failures in libmultiprocess, making CI coverage on this architecture desirable. It affects only CI test coverage.
evidence: Commit 65ddcb4f35: 'Exercise IPC on 32-bit x86, where compiler ABI differences have caused failures.'
Description: 'It was chosen arbitrarily in #31802 to have coverage for -DENABLE_IPC=OFF, but this was not a good choice given issues like: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/383'
problem: Disabling IPC on 32-bit x86 CI runs leaves 32-bit IPC support untested in CI, allowing architecture- and compiler-specific ABI bugs (such as those previously found in libmultiprocess) to slip past CI undetected.

risk.why: Only alters CI configuration to enable IPC on the i686 test runner.

scope_notes: Small CI configuration adjustment (+6/-5 lines across 2 files). Diff was not provided.
summary: Enables IPC testing in the 32-bit x86 (i686) continuous integration job. The job previously explicitly disabled IPC to provide build coverage for -DENABLE_IPC=OFF, but 32-bit platforms have specific ABI differences that need testing under IPC. Other platforms like Windows and RISC-V continue to build without IPC enabled.
